slides.headline: One kiss. Then this masterpiece vanished.
Night in the garden
slides.text: Night, in the garden of Gethsemane. Caravaggio crowds everyone into one tight, dark frame, so close you feel pushed into the scene.

slides.headline: The kiss
slides.text: Judas has just kissed Jesus. It was the signal for the soldiers: the man I kiss is the one you want.

slides.headline: Clasped hands
slides.text: Jesus does not fight back. His face is sad, his hands clasped, while the arrest closes in around him.

slides.headline: Shining armour
slides.text: In the centre, a soldier's polished armour shines like a mirror. Cold metal, grabbing a man in plain clothes.

slides.headline: Running away
slides.text: On the far left, a young follower, John, screams and runs, as a soldier grabs his cloak.

slides.headline: The lantern
slides.text: And on the right, a man raises a lantern to see better. Experts believe it is Caravaggio himself, watching the betrayal.

slides.headline: Lost
slides.text: Then the painting disappeared from view. For two centuries, people thought it was only a copy by a Dutch painter, Honthorst.

slides.headline: Found in Dublin
slides.text: In the early 1990s, a restorer recognised it in a Jesuit house in Dublin. How many masterpieces still hide in plain sight?
